Let \( a_0, a_1, a_2, \ldots \) be the unique sequence of nonnegative integers less than 397 with \( a_0 = 1 \) and

\[ a_{n+1}(a_n + 1)^2 \equiv a_n \pmod{397} \]

for all nonnegative integers \( n \). Given that \( a_{2026} = 9 \), compute the remainder when \( a_0 + a_1 + \cdots + a_{2026} \) is divided by 397.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
All congruences are modulo \(397\).

Since \(a_{2026}=9\), no term \(a_n\) with \(0\le n\le 2026\) can be \(0\); if \(a_k=0\), then the recurrence forces all later terms to be \(0\). Since \(397\) is prime, each \(a_n\) in this range has a modular inverse.

Define

\[
T_n=a_n+a_n^{-1}.
\]

From

\[
a_{n+1}(a_n+1)^2\equiv a_n,
\]

invert \(a_{n+1}\):

\[
a_{n+1}^{-1}\equiv \frac{(a_n+1)^2}{a_n}
= a_n+2+a_n^{-1}
= T_n+2.
\]

Therefore,

\[
T_{n+1}=a_{n+1}+a_{n+1}^{-1}
\equiv a_{n+1}+T_n+2,
\]

so

\[
a_{n+1}\equiv T_{n+1}-T_n-2.
\]

Thus the sum telescopes:

\[
\begin{aligned}
a_0+a_1+\cdots+a_{2026}
&=a_0+\sum_{n=0}^{2025}(T_{n+1}-T_n-2)\\
&=1+(T_{2026}-T_0)-2\cdot 2026.
\end{aligned}
\]

Since \(a_0=1\),

\[
T_0=1+1=2.
\]

Also,

\[
T_{2026}=a_{2026}+a_{2026}^{-1}=9+9^{-1}.
\]

Because \(9\cdot 353=3177\equiv 1\pmod{397}\), we have \(9^{-1}\equiv 353\), so

\[
T_{2026}\equiv 9+353=362.
\]

Hence

\[
a_0+\cdots+a_{2026}
\equiv 362-2-4052
=362-4053.
\]

Now \(4053\equiv 83\pmod{397}\), so

\[
362-4053\equiv 362-83=279\pmod{397}.
\]

\[
\boxed{279}
\]
